clue.text: Ardent Tory from the right is depressed

parts.note: right in the sense of correct or accurate means true
feeling depressed is feeling blue

explanation.surface: A passionate Conservative, being right-wing, is feeling glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the right' looks like a political direction, but 'right' just means correct, TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative party colour, so a staunch, loyal Conservative is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Hasten the day when it flattens the stomach!

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the day a slimming garment arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to wish time forward ('bring on the weekend'), and is also an elasticated girdle or corset that slims the waist.

clue.text: In summer I can roam the heath

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the run of words summer I can

explanation.surface: In the summer months I'm free to wander over the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heathers, plants also called heath.

clue.text: Ridiculous arrangement withdrew from

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Ridiculous arrangement withdrew from', has no fodder giving LUDICROUS (it would need CURIOUS plus L and D); OCR seems garbled and no scan or search gives the printed clue.

clue.text: Write coded message in French vault

parts.note: the French word for in is en
a vault under a church is a crypt

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles a secret note while hiding in a French church vault.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a message into a cipher is to scramble it into code.

clue.text: Dash away when the lemonade is finished

parts.note: fizzy lemonade is a type of pop, a soft drink
finished, as with food all gone or a match over, is off

explanation.surface: A child runs off once the fizzy drink has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrasal verb means to leave quickly or suddenly; it can also mean to die.

clue.text: Party leader moves to make treaties

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Party

parts.note: moves, as steps taken, are acts

explanation.surface: A political boss makes overtures to sign international agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like a politician, but it is just the first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal agreements between nations, also called pacts.

clue.text: Award custom, but be condescending

explanation.surface: Give a shop your business while treating its staff with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a shop your regular trade is one sense; to speak down to someone with superior kindness is the other.

clue.text: Regina's immersion in novels creates discord

indicators.note: immersion in places one piece inside another, as if dunked into it

parts.note: novels collectively are fiction
R is the abbreviation for Regina, Latin for queen, as in royal cyphers

explanation.surface: A queen absorbed in reading stories causes arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for Regina (queen), as in ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is disagreement or conflict, a synonym of discord.

clue.text: Everything that is done initially in co-operation

parts.note: everything is all
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of done

explanation.surface: Everything, that is, was achieved through working together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations joined in alliance work together, so allied describes acting in partnership.

clue.text: Possibly the white lady in the bar

definitions.text: Possibly the white lady in the bar

parts.words: Possibly the white lady in the bar
parts.note: reads as a pale woman sitting in a pub, but White Lady is a gin-based mixed drink served there

explanation.surface: A pale woman may be found sitting in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A White Lady is a mixed drink of gin, orange liqueur and lemon juice; 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Lady is one example of a mixed alcoholic drink ordered at a bar.

clue.text: My anchor, sadly is in such a state

indicators.note: sadly, as in in a sorry, wrecked condition, marks the letters as rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor laments that their anchor is in a sorry condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by a king or queen is a kingdom of this kind, as the UK is.

clue.text: Goes in search of college servants

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for the staff who clean college rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford University a scout is a college servant who cleans and tidies students' rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconnoitre or look around for something is one sense; at Oxford, college servants who look after students' rooms are the other.

clue.text: Made Doris protest to leading journalist

indicators.note: Made, as in made into something else, signals a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Doris was forced to complain to a senior figure at the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor of a newspaper's sports pages is a senior journalist heading that section.

clue.text: There's drink available-but not champagne!

parts.note: reads as a host apologising there's no bubbly, but describes table wine without fizz, still meaning not sparkling

explanation.surface: A host apologises that there's plenty to drink, just no bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine without bubbles, as opposed to sparkling wine such as champagne.

clue.text: Like Elgar's Variations or the Mona Lisa's smile

definitions.text: Like Elgar's Variations or the Mona Lisa's smile

parts.words: Like Elgar's Variations or the Mona Lisa's smile
parts.note: Elgar's orchestral Variations bear the title Enigma, and Leonardo's portrait is famous for its mysterious smile

explanation.surface: A comparison between a famous English orchestral work and Leonardo's famous portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mysterious: Elgar's work hides a puzzle theme, and the portrait's expression is famously inscrutable.

clue.text: Lovely lady in a hat is satirised unfairly

indicators.note: in places the lovely lady inside the hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A pretty woman in a bonnet is unkindly mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is a damaging false written statement, so someone defamed in print has been unjustly lampooned.

clue.text: Kind of help expected from government bureaux

explanation.surface: The sort of assistance one hopes to get from state offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as polite help, it is courteous assistance; as a phrase it is the permanent body of government departments and officials.

clue.text: Quoted and quoted again

explanation.surface: Something said aloud, then repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken from memory, as a poem, is one sense; read as re-cited, it means cited a second time.

clue.text: Dave is ordered to offer counsel

indicators.note: ordered, as in put into a new order, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dave has been told to give guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to recommend a course of action or give guidance.

clue.text: He had imbibed beer to be revivified

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the beer goes inside the other piece

parts.note: He had contracts to he'd
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: After drinking beer, a man felt restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He had' contracts to HE'D, which takes in ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brought back to health or life is cured or made whole again.

clue.text: Outline scheme for American conscription

explanation.surface: A rough plan for US military call-up.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US the draft is military conscription (the British say call-up).
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary sketch or plan is one sense; in the US, compulsory enlistment into the armed forces is another.

clue.text: Shock troops charge round

parts.note: having charge of something is having command of it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Assault soldiers storm around the position.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are elite soldiers trained for raids; the word names both the soldier and the unit.

clue.text: Old historian rendered account with style

parts.note: ton means fashionable style, from French

explanation.surface: A past chronicler gave an elegant report.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Acton was a Victorian historian, known for 'power tends to corrupt'. 'Ton' is an old word for fashion or style.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dalberg-Acton was a nineteenth-century English historian at Cambridge.

clue.text: One beset by insistent petitioner

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: clamant means insistent, noisily demanding
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is besieged by a persistent person filing a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person asserting a right or making a claim in court is a petitioner.

clue.text: Tasty morsel birdie pecked at

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a birdie
a bird that pecked at something bit it

explanation.surface: A small bird pecked at a delicious scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small delicacy or choice piece of food.

clue.text: Coming shortly before Christmas

explanation.surface: Something is arriving just ahead of the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival; it is also the church season of the four weeks before Christmas.

clue.text: Can't go into action whilst being rehoused

indicators.note: go into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
the contraction can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they can't act while being moved to a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: Councils speak of tenants being decanted: moved out to new homes while theirs are repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Decanting means pouring into another vessel, used figuratively of moving people to other housing.
